## Symptom

When a collapse replays any commit above the boundary, the ledger-anchor commit is not an ancestor of the rewritten tip. The rewritten branch runs checkpoint → first replayed commit. The ledger anchor is a side child of the checkpoint that nothing references, and the collapse deletes its scratch ref, so the anchor ends up unreachable.

`CollapseResult.enforce_since` is that anchor. `verify_authorship._is_enforced` (`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py:258`) enforces an event only when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <since_ref> <event commit>` succeeds. That never happens for an unreachable anchor, so every event in the rewritten history is grandfathered. `verify-identity` then passes without checking any signature.

## Evidence

- **Synthetic probe, 2026-11-17.** Built from `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py::_build_collapsible_store`, with 1 replayed commit. The result was `anchor_is_ancestor_of_tip False` and `enforce_since == ledger_anchor_sha True`. The same result came from the current engine (origin/main 57d45053272) and from the original S1 engine (a758402f065, ticket `filmable-crushing-nighthawk`). The defect predates the streamed rewrite (`silk-unpleasant-jackal`), which reproduced the original behaviour exactly.
- **Real-scale dry run, 2026-11-16.** On a TMPDIR copy of `origin/tickets` at e7a0476397f, the rewritten root 9ecfe8768a5 has exactly one child, b04372602ca. That child is a replayed `reconciler: persist binding-store snapshot` commit. `git log --grep "reconcile authorship ledger" tickets` finds nothing.
- **Why the existing test passes.** `test_enforce_since_reanchor_makes_verify_authorship_clean` collapses with the tip equal to the boundary. No commit is replayed, so the anchor is the tip and the defect is hidden.

## Cause

In `_StreamedRewrite._replay` (`src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py:507`), a replayed commit's parents go through `self.old_to_new`, and `_write_base` maps the boundary to the checkpoint (`self._map(boundary, self.checkpoint_sha)`). A replayed commit whose original parent is the boundary is therefore parented on the checkpoint, not on the ledger anchor (`self.current_tip` at that point).

## Approach

In `_replay`, map a parent equal to the boundary to `self.ledger_anchor_sha` instead of `old_to_new[boundary]`. Leave `old_to_new[boundary] = checkpoint_sha` unchanged. The SNAPSHOT ledger rewrites (`_map_old_commit`) still resolve below-boundary events to the checkpoint, which stays an ancestor of every rewritten commit through the anchor.

The anchor's tree is the boundary tree plus the re-resolved SNAPSHOTs. Its `source_of` is already the boundary, and its `k_of` is 0. A child of the anchor therefore diffs against the boundary and inherits the anchor's rewritten SNAPSHOT bytes. It re-resolves only the SNAPSHOTs that reference commits mapped after the anchor, which is the same dirty rule the engine already applies.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/reclaim_collapse.py`: the parent mapping in `_StreamedRewrite._replay`.
- `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py`: the regression tests below.

## Testing

TDD, red first, on throwaway shadow repositories under `tmp_path`.

- Ancestry: after `_build_collapsible_store` plus an applied collapse (1 replayed commit), `git merge-base --is-ancestor <ledger_anchor_sha> HEAD` succeeds and the anchor is the first parent of the first replayed commit.
- Enforcement: an unsigned replayed event fails `python -m rebar verify-identity --all` under `REBAR_IDENTITY_REQUIRE_AUTHENTICATED=1` and `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE=<enforce_since>` (exit non-zero, the event counted unsigned). Below-boundary events stay grandfathered. This is the failure path the existing test cannot see.
- `test_streamed_engine_matches_the_rewrite_oracle` keeps passing. Its expectations are parent counts and SNAPSHOT SHA mappings, and both still hold.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] After a collapse that replays at least one commit, `ledger_anchor_sha` is an ancestor of `rewritten_tip`, and `enforce_since` names a commit on the rewritten branch. The new ancestry test shows this.
- [x] With replayed commits and `REBAR_IDENTITY_ENFORCE_SINCE=<enforce_since>`, `verify-identity --all` enforces the replayed events. The new enforcement test shows an unsigned replayed event failing the gate.
- [x] Every test in `tests/unit/test_reclaim_collapse.py` passes.
- [x] `make verify` is run and any failure is fixed or shown environmental; the Gerrit change gets `Verified +1`; `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` and `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exit 0.
